gcollapse

Collapse group means using the gcollapse workflow

Stata 

gcollapse (mean) z=x, by(g)

R dplyr 

data <- dplyr::summarise(data,z=mean(x,na.rm=TRUE),.by=g)

Stata reference · R reference

Keep raw group row counts beside collapsed means

Stata 

gcollapse (mean) z=x, by(g) freq(n)

R dplyr 

data <- dplyr::summarise(data,z=mean(x,na.rm=TRUE),n=dplyr::n(),.by=g)

Stata reference · R reference

Add collapsed group means back to all original rows

Stata 

gcollapse (mean) z=x, by(g) merge

R dplyr 

data <- dplyr::mutate(data,z=mean(x,na.rm=TRUE),.by=g)

Stata reference · R reference

Collapse group missing-value counts

Stata 

gcollapse (nmissing) n=x, by(g)

R dplyr 

data <- dplyr::summarise(data,n=sum(is.na(x)),.by=g)

Stata reference · R reference

Collapse group distinct-value counts on complete data

Stata 

gcollapse (nunique) n=x, by(g)

R dplyr 

data <- dplyr::summarise(data,n=dplyr::n_distinct(x,na.rm=TRUE),.by=g)

Differs from Stata Complete values in this fixture; treatment of missing categories is not asserted.

Stata reference · R reference

gcontract

Count jointly observed category combinations

Stata 

gcontract g h, freq(n)

R dplyr 

data <- dplyr::count(data,g,h,name='n')

Stata reference · R reference

Create category counts and percentages with gcontract

Stata 

gcontract g, freq(n) percent(p)

R dplyr 

data <- dplyr::count(data,g,name='n'); data$p <- 100*data$n/sum(data$n)

Stata reference · R reference

gdistinct

Count distinct values separately for several columns

Stata 

gdistinct g h

R base 

vapply(data[c('g','h')],function(z) length(unique(z[!is.na(z)])),integer(1))

Stata reference · R reference

Count distinct complete combinations jointly

Stata 

gdistinct g h, joint

R base 

nrow(unique(data[stats::complete.cases(data[c('g','h')]),c('g','h')]))

Stata reference · R reference

gduplicates

Keep the first row of each compound key

Stata 

gduplicates drop g h, force

R base 

data <- data[!duplicated(data[c('g','h')]),,drop=FALSE]

Stata reference · R reference

Tag all duplicates of compound keys

Stata 

gduplicates tag g h, generate(dup)

R dplyr 

data <- dplyr::mutate(data,dup=dplyr::n()-1L,.by=c(g,h))

Stata reference · R reference

gegen

Create identifiers for complete combinations of keys

Stata 

gegen groupid = group(g h)

R base 

data$groupid <- as.integer(interaction(data$g,data$h,drop=TRUE,lex.order=TRUE))

Differs from Stata Complete numeric keys only; exact identifier ordering follows the demonstrated lexicographic keys.

Stata reference · R reference

Tag one observation in each nonmissing group

Stata 

gegen tag = tag(g)

R base 

data$tag <- as.integer(!is.na(data$g)&!duplicated(data$g))

Stata reference · R reference

Attach group means using a gegen-style workflow

Stata 

gegen z = mean(x), by(g)

R dplyr 

data <- dplyr::mutate(data,z=mean(x,na.rm=TRUE),.by=g)

Stata reference · R reference

generate

Create a binary indicator retaining missing values

Stata 

generate byte high = x > 3 if x < .

R dplyr 

data <- dplyr::mutate(data, high = as.integer(x > 3))

Comparisons with NA return NA, matching the if x < . restriction.

Stata reference · R reference

Create a nonmissing indicator

Stata 

generate byte observed = !missing(x)

R dplyr 

data <- dplyr::mutate(data, observed = as.integer(!is.na(x)))

Stata reference · R reference

Create a running sum ignoring missing values

Stata 

generate cumulative = sum(x)

R base 

data$cumulative <- cumsum(replace(data$x,is.na(data$x),0))

Stata's generate sum() treats missing contributions as zero, unlike raw cumsum().

generate double z = x^2

R dplyr 

data <- dplyr::mutate(data, z = x^2)

Stata reference · R reference

Create row numbers

Stata 

generate row = _n

R dplyr 

data <- dplyr::mutate(data, row = dplyr::row_number())

Number observations within sorted groups

Stata 

bysort g (id): generate row = _n

R dplyr 

data <- dplyr::arrange(data,g,id); data <- dplyr::mutate(data,row=dplyr::row_number(),.by=g)

bysort g (id): generate total = sum(x)

R dplyr 

data <- dplyr::arrange(data,g,id); data <- dplyr::mutate(data,total=cumsum(replace(x,is.na(x),0)),.by=g)

Attach group row counts

R dplyr

Stata reference · R reference

Mark the first observation within sorted groups

Stata 

bysort id (year): generate first = _n == 1

R dplyr 

{ data <- dplyr::arrange(data, id, year); dplyr::mutate(data, first = as.integer(dplyr::row_number() == 1L), .by = id) }

Differs from Stata Sorts by id and year, then marks one first row per id, including a missing-id group. Ties in year use input order in R; add a tie-break variable for a reproducible cross-system choice.

gisid

Validate compound-key uniqueness allowing ordinary missing

Stata 

gisid g h, missok

R base 

stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(data[c('g','h')]))

Differs from Stata Ordinary missing is allowed as a key value; extended Stata missing categories are not represented here.

Stata reference · R reference

Assert a unique complete identifier with gisid

Stata 

gisid id

R base 

stopifnot(!anyNA(data$id),!anyDuplicated(data$id))

Stata reference · R reference

glevelsof

List distinct complete multi-column keys

Stata 

glevelsof g h

R base 

levels <- unique(data[c('g','h')]); levels <- levels[do.call(order,levels),,drop=FALSE]

Differs from Stata Returns a key table rather than a space-delimited local macro; fixture keys contain no missing values.

Stata reference · R reference

Store sorted distinct categories with glevelsof

Stata 

glevelsof g, local(levels)

R base 

levels <- sort(unique(data$g[!is.na(data$g)]))

Stata reference · R reference

gquantiles

Assign four empirical quantile categories

Stata 

gquantiles quartile=x, xtile nquantiles(4)

R base 

cuts <- stats::quantile(data$x,c(.25,.5,.75),type=2); data$quartile <- as.integer(cut(data$x,breaks=c(-Inf,cuts,Inf),right=TRUE))

Differs from Stata Unweighted distinct finite values; uses explicit R type-2 cutoffs and right-closed categories. Ties can prevent equal group sizes.

Stata reference · R reference

Return selected empirical percentile cutpoints

Stata 

gquantiles x, _pctile percentiles(25 50 75)

R base 

stats::quantile(data$x,c(.25,.5,.75),type=2)

Differs from Stata Explicit R type-2 unweighted percentile workflow; no alternative-definition or weighted numerical parity is asserted.

Stata reference · R reference

greshape

Gather explicitly named wide columns with greshape

Stata 

greshape gather x1 x2, keys(measure) values(value)

R tidyr 

data <- tidyr::pivot_longer(data,c(x1,x2),names_to='measure',values_to='value')

Stata reference · R reference

Drop missing measurements while reshaping one stub

Stata 

greshape long x, by(id) keys(wave) dropmiss

R tidyr 

data <- tidyr::pivot_longer(data,c(x1,x2),names_to='wave',names_prefix='x',names_transform=list(wave=as.integer),values_to='x',values_drop_na=TRUE)

Differs from Stata Single-stub fixed workflow; for multiple stubs drop a row only when every reshaped value is missing.

Stata reference · R reference

Spread text-keyed values into columns with greshape

Stata 

greshape spread value, keys(measure)

R tidyr 

data <- tidyr::pivot_wider(data,names_from=measure,values_from=value)

Stata reference · R reference

gsort

Sort descending with Stata missing first

Stata 

gsort -x

R dplyr 

data <- dplyr::arrange(data, !is.na(x), dplyr::desc(x))

Sorting on !is.na(x) first places missing values at the top, as gsort does.

Stata reference · R reference

Sort by ascending group and descending value

Stata 

gsort g -y

R dplyr 

data <- dplyr::arrange(data, g, dplyr::desc(y))

Stata reference · R reference

1 more examples and alternatives

Sort descending with Stata missing first

Stata 

gsort -x

R base 

data <- data[order(-data$x,na.last=FALSE), , drop=FALSE]

Numeric missing sorts first in Stata descending order; use na.last=FALSE deliberately.

Stata reference · R reference

gstats

Cap tails separately inside each group

Stata 

gstats winsor x, by(g) cuts(25 75) replace

R dplyr 

data <- dplyr::mutate(data,x={b <- stats::quantile(x,c(.25,.75),na.rm=TRUE,type=2); pmax(b[1],pmin(b[2],x))},.by=g)

Differs from Stata Groups use independent unweighted R type-2 cutoffs; all-missing groups require an explicit policy.

Stata reference · R reference

Cap both tails at explicitly selected empirical quartiles

Stata 

gstats winsor x, cuts(25 75) generate(z)

R base 

bounds <- stats::quantile(data$x,c(.25,.75),na.rm=TRUE,type=2); data$z <- pmax(bounds[1],pmin(bounds[2],data$x))

Differs from Stata Unweighted workflow with an explicit R type-2 empirical percentile rule; no cross-software numerical certification is claimed.

Stata reference · R reference

Set values outside empirical quartiles to missing

Stata 

gstats winsor x, cuts(25 75) trim generate(z)

R base 

bounds <- stats::quantile(data$x,c(.25,.75),na.rm=TRUE,type=2); data$z <- data$x; data$z[!is.na(data$x) & (data$x<bounds[1] | data$x>bounds[2])] <- NA_real_

Differs from Stata Trimming sets tails to missing while retaining rows; percentile rule is explicit R type 2 and no weighted parity is asserted.

Stata reference · R reference

gtoplevelsof

Find the two most frequent complete categories

Stata 

gtoplevelsof g, ntop(2)

R dplyr 

counts <- dplyr::count(data,g,name='n'); counts <- counts[order(-counts$n,counts$g),]; top <- utils::head(counts,2)

Differs from Stata Returns the leading categories and counts only; Stata cumulative/Other rows are not generated. gtop is an alias and is not counted separately.

Count unique complete row-key combinations

Stata 

gunique g h

R base 

nrow(unique(data[c('g','h')]))

Differs from Stata Complete keys in this fixture; unlike gdistinct without joint, gunique treats all listed columns jointly.

Stata 

gunique h, by(g) generate(nunique)

data <- dplyr::mutate(data,nunique=dplyr::n_distinct(h),.by=g)

Differs from Stata Complete group and value columns in this example; no missing-category behavior is asserted.

hashsort

Stably sort by ascending group and descending value

Stata 

hashsort g -x

R base 

data <- data[order(data$g,-data$x,method='radix'),,drop=FALSE]

Differs from Stata Complete numeric keys only; R radix sort preserves original order for equal keys. No comparative speed claim is made.

insobs

Insert a missing row after a position

Stata 

insobs 1, after(2)

R base 

data <- rbind(data[seq_len(2),,drop=FALSE],data[NA_integer_,,drop=FALSE],data[-seq_len(2),,drop=FALSE])
